HD 169142 is a nearby (114.0 pc) F1 star hosting an almost face on (inclination of 13$^{\circ}$, position angle of 5$^{\circ}$) protoplanetary disk (cite: 2006AJ....131.2290R; 2017A&A...600A..72F; 2018A&A...616A...1G; 2018A&A...620A.128V).

HD 169142 is a nearby (114.0 pc) F1 star hosting an almost face on (inclination of 13$^{\circ}$, position angle of 5$^{\circ}$) protoplanetary disk (cite: 2006AJ....131.2290R; 2017A&A...600A..72F; 2018A&A...616A...1G; 2018A&A...620A.128V).

In this paper, we present Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the HD 169142 disk where we detect 13 different species. Using these data, we infer the elemental make-up of the gas and location of both the CO and snowlines in relation to these forming planets.

We have compiled ALMA observations towards the HD 169142 disk over Bands 6, 7 and 8.
These observations consist of 5 spectral windows with 3 dedicated to the CO lines (, , $J=2-1$) and two continuum windows centred at 218.004 GHz and 232.004 GHz.

The dataset contains four spectral windows, which are centred at 478.651 GHz, 480.568 GHz, 489.785 GHz and 492.195 GHz with the latter two the line spectral windows at $\sim0.15$ km s$^{-1}$ spectral resolution.

Four spectral windows were used, centred at 279.515 GHz (resolution of $\sim0.15$ km s$^{-1}$), 277.990 GHz ($\sim1.2$ km s$^{-1}$), 288.147 GHz ($\sim0.29$ km s$^{-1}$) and 289.990 GHz ($\sim17$ km s$^{-1}$).

This comparison and the temperature structure in the disk model from (cite: 2018A&A...614A.106C) indicates the lack of CO freeze-out in the HD 169142 disk but, if there is a CO freeze-out in this disk it is likely beyond the mm-dust disk edge ($\approx$100 au) and out at $\approx$150 au.
The detection of and from the inner disk can be explained by the sublimation of ices putting the snowline at the edge of the inner mm-dust $\approx$20 au.
Since needs to form in the cold phase, this further supports the hypothesis that complex ices can survive the disk formation process.

We estimate that the giant planet HD 169142 b is forming between the and snowlines and given the temperature structure of the disks likely between the and snowlines. This is a region of the disk where C/O$\approx$1.0.
If there is another giant planet in the central cavity $<$20 au this is within the snowline and therefore the planet will be accreting gas with C/O$<$1.

Comparing to the models presented in (cite: 2019ApJ...881..127A) and (cite: 2022ApJ...926L...2T) the low line flux observed towards HD 169142 relative to is consistent with minimal CO depletion, i.e., a gas-phase CO/ abundance of $\approx10^{-4}$.
Scaled to a distance of 100 pc the emission from HD 169142 is $\approx$10$\times$ weaker than in both of the Herbig disks and the T-Tauri disk TW Hya.
